note: Config for the Actionable Market Brief cockpit: machine-readable universe + deep-link map + update windows + thresholds + an agent-maintained macro-events list + a standing global/geopolitical backdrop. All analytics are computed LIVE from the shared rlData cache; nothing here is a stored analytic. STRUCTURE FIRST, NOISE LAST: the brief anchors every read in the larger picture (20/50/200 MA, 126/252d trend, macro cycle, global tensions, what's priced in) and never flips a call on a single-window intraday micro-delta (see notes/market-brief.md §6c). track.groups holds the thematic mega-cap / semis baskets (Mag 7 proxied by MAGS, semis by SOXX) — Tier-A computes the group ETF read + each member + breadth, and the agent elevates the NOTABLE members per run (see §7a). The agent follows notes/market-brief.md. Educational only — not investment advice.

windows.label: Pre-market
windows.focus: next-session actions first: overnight/pre-market gaps, Asia/Europe/global rotation, GLD/BTC/commodities, today's events + option-implied moves, and exact levels to act on at the open

windows.label: Morning
windows.focus: only what changes today's plan: did the open hold/reject key levels, rotation/real-asset confirmation, intraday breadth, and next-session risk

windows.label: Pre-close
windows.focus: tomorrow-first positioning: actions into the close, gamma pin/magnet, hold/trim/hedge overnight, global/real-asset confirmation, and tomorrow's catalysts

windows.label: After-hours
windows.focus: next-trading-day plan: after-hours reactions, persistent regime/rotation/global/real-asset changes, exact triggers/invalidation, and overnight risk

groups.label: Magnificent 7
groups.desc: The seven mega-caps that dominate index returns, proxied by the Roundhill MAGS ETF. The group read = leading/lagging vs SPY + the 20/50/200-day MA stack; breadth = how many of the 7 are individually bull-stacked. Notable/moving members are elevated per run (§7a). Members mirror the sector-lab MAG7 basket.

groups.label: Semiconductors
groups.desc: The semiconductor complex, proxied by the iShares SOXX ETF — the AI-capex 'build-it' side that leads/lags mega-cap software. Group read + breadth + notable-member elevation per run (§7a). The brief uses SOXX; the sector lab's own SEMIS basket keeps its SMH proxy.

output-budget/v1.rationaleDecisionNote: DECIDED 2026-08-20, closing the open question the previous note left. attention[].rationale STAYS OUT of defaultVisibleFields: it is the detail a reader opens deliberately, and the brief's stated shape is a short card whose detail is hidden by default and available on demand. Folding it in was measured and rejected — the published VGT item measures 194 against the 300 decisionCardChars cap, its rationale measures 575, and the two together measure 769, so the very next recompose would have refused the only item the feed was publishing. What was actually wrong is that a hidden field was bounded NOWHERE and could grow without limit. detailFieldChars now bounds it. 700 is set above the observed maximum of 575 across 12 published rationales (min 284, median 461) so nothing already authored breaches it, and deliberately not at 600: a per-card breach discards the WHOLE narrative, and this packet has already seen 14 characters cost an entire brief. The lane is told the cap and told to aim well under it, so the bound is satisfiable rather than a trap.
output-budget/v1.badgeMeasurementNote: ADDED 2026-08-22, found by opening the page rather than by a gate. dataAsOf.labels.bars and dataAsOf.labels.macro render into the header badge ABOVE every decision — the most prominent text on the cockpit — and were absent from this list, so the budget whose entire purpose is bounding the default view never measured its most visible element. The badge was rendering the FULL dataAsOf.* narratives at 3,266 characters until the renderer was pointed at the condensed labels; even condensed it is 1,173. Only the two fields the badge actually renders are declared here, which is both semantically right (this list is the default-VISIBLE surface) and non-destructive: measured total moves 887 -> 2,060 against the 3,000 cap, whereas declaring all four labels would total 3,424 and breach on the next publish. No per-field cap is set in the same change that first states the contract, for the reason the confidence contract records: state it, observe a run, then tighten. The 3,000 total is the live enforcement and leaves 940 characters of headroom.
output-budget/v1.note: Caps OUTPUT. artifact-budget/v1 caps FETCH. Neither may be raised inside a change that would otherwise fail against it. The measurement sums String.length over the paths above and counts no key, no number, no boolean, no null and no field outside the list; everything else in the payload is reported once as disclosedTotal and is never capped. Raising a cap to rescue a failing run is a separate owner decision recorded in notes/market-brief.md, never part of the change that would have failed.

attention-detection-policy/v1.authorship: DRAFTED BY AGENT on 2026-08-19 under explicit operator delegation, and NOT yet owner-tuned. These numbers decide when the brief interrupts you, which is a statement about your risk tolerance and not a fact about any market. They are deliberately conservative so the first failure mode is silence rather than noise. Tune THESE NUMBERS, never rlattentiongate.js: the module holds no thresholds and refuses to observe anything when this block is absent or incomplete.
attention-detection-policy/v1.severityBandsNote: Read against the subject's percentage distance from its 200-day moving average. A reading under the narrowest band produces NO observation at all rather than a 'mild' one, which is how a quiet day stays quiet. 'mild' is left undeclared on purpose: nothing in this repository has yet earned the right to interrupt a reader at that size.
attention-detection-policy/v1.measuredBaseline: MEASURED 2026-08-20 against the 201 snapshots in brief-history.jsonl, so a later tuning decision starts from evidence rather than from the conservative intent above. At the current minAbsPct 8, 88.1% of subject-days across the 12 mapped subjects already clear the band and 191 of 201 snapshots carry at least one eligible subject; lowering it to 6 moves that to 94.7% and to 4 moves it to 96.4%. These bands are therefore NEAR-SATURATED, not conservative, and the 'first failure mode is silence' intent is not what these particular numbers are producing.
attention-detection-policy/v1.measuredBaselineLever: A quiet feed is NOT evidence that these numbers are too tight, and widening them is unlikely to add a single item. recomposePayloadAttention starts from payload.attention — the items the signals lane AUTHORED — and transmissionBySubject is only ever a lookup for a named subject, never enumerated to propose one. The band can therefore subtract from what the lane wrote but can never add to it. On the live payload the composer reported '1 built, 0 refused': the gate refused nothing, so a wider band would have admitted nothing. If the feed should carry more items, the lever is how many candidates the signals lane authors, not these thresholds.
attention-detection-policy/v1.sourceToolNote: The tool that OWNS the math this policy reads. A gate's figures cite it as their provenance, which is also how the composer resolves the item's deep link — so a reader can open the tool that produced the number. Declared here rather than hard-coded because the owning tool is a property of where the math lives, and that can move.
attention-detection-policy/v1.imminenceNote: Distance to the 200-day, the level this policy watches. Sitting within 2% of it is 'imminent' because the level is in play now; out to 6% is 'developing'; beyond that the reading is real but 'latent'.
attention-detection-policy/v1.transmissionNote: The channel an effect would travel, drawn from the certified vocabulary in rlmarketaction.js. A subject missing from this map declares NO channel rather than a guessed one; when such a subject is also imminent, the gate says so explicitly instead of implying a path it cannot name.
attention-detection-policy/v1.gaps: Rates and the dollar are NOT in this map, and that is a real gap rather than an oversight: the brief's rates leg resolves through TLT and its dollar leg is dark by governance, so a policy row for them would promise an observation the data layer cannot supply today. Adding them is a data-layer change first, a policy change second.

legs.label: Dollar
legs.withheld: No broad-dollar direction is stated this run, so nothing in the brief leans on the dollar.

legs.label: Credit
legs.withheld: Whether credit is confirming or contradicting the equity trend is not stated.

cross-asset/v1.note: Three REQUIRED slots — rates, dollar, energy — each present on every published run and each resolving to exactly one of a reading or a dark state. Credit is a fourth, non-required leg: it is published when the bond model offers a classification to carry and omitted when it does not, and its absence never fails the required set. A measured leg makes an INSTRUMENT-level claim only: it reports its own driver's price change over `sessions` and never renames that instrument as the concept it tracks, so the rates leg is the TLT price and never 'the yield curve', and the energy leg is the USO price and never 'crude'. Both drivers are declared by real-assets-universe.json, which is what puts them in reach of the bars map buildRealAssetsToolRead builds; a committed data/bars file is not the admission test. The dollar leg is DARK BY GOVERNANCE and declares no driver on purpose: fx-regime-universe.json admits no broad-dollar evidence source (fed-h10-unavailable is denied, broad-proxy-unreviewed is unreviewed with persistence forbidden), so no broad-dollar index or proxy figure may be published in any form and the dark reason is the sentence buildFxToolRead already emits rather than one composed here. Raising a leg out of dark by widening a universe or approving a proxy is a separate owner decision, never part of a change that would otherwise publish an inadmissible reading.

flagProducers.earningsWithinWindow: nearTermEvents in rlexperience-adapters/market-action.js against the committed events[]

change-vocabulary/v1.note: The CLOSED set of things the brief is willing to call a change. An instrument earns per-instrument narrative only when changeKind returns a member of `kinds`; everything else is counted into one roll-up line and never restated as a paragraph. A kind outside this list is a refusal, never a silent pass-through. `precedence` makes the single-kind-per-instrument rule deterministic when more than one predicate fires, and it deliberately omits `baseline`, which is not a predicate but the answer to an absent prior row. `baseline` is NOT `unchanged`: calling an instrument the brief has never seen before unchanged is a false statement about the past, so the roll-up counts the two separately and the balance is narrative + unchanged + baseline === trackedSet.length. Each declared flag reuses the producer named in `flagProducers` and this vocabulary declares no second producer; a call opening is flagRaised on callOpen and a call closing is flagCleared on it, so the vocabulary stays closed rather than growing an opened/closed pair. `levels` names the thresholds.maWindows values plus the 52-week range the structural block already spans, and a crossing is a sign change of px minus the level on BOTH sides, so a level a run cannot compute is an absence and never a crossing. `trackedSet` mirrors watchlist.json; the roll-up balance is asserted against its length, so adding a ticker here without adding it to the watchlist is refused by the balance rather than silently dropped.

freshness-policy/v1.note: The narrative (Tier-B) is operator-hosted and can silently stop refreshing, and a brief that quietly serves last week's read as if it were this morning's is the single most damaging thing this product can do. Thresholds allow for the legitimate gaps in a four-window weekday schedule: the largest normal overnight gap is 17:00 ET to 07:30 ET (~14.5h), so warnAfterHours 18 does not fire on a healthy night; a Friday-close to Monday-open weekend is ~62h, so staleAfterHours 72 does not fire on a healthy weekend. Past those, the page says so in a banner rather than letting the reader infer freshness from a timestamp they will not check. An absent payload is NOT treated as fresh - it renders the explicit 'narrative not refreshed this window' state.

scorecard-policy/v1.note: Governs market-brief.scorecard.json. Below minResolvedSample the hit rate is WITHHELD and the sample size is shown instead - a rate over a handful of calls is noise dressed as evidence. recentMissCount misses are always published in full alongside the hits; selective reporting is the one unrecoverable failure for this product. not-evaluable is reported as its own share and never counted as a win.
